title: My Impression of Keigo Higashino
description: Keigo Higashino dies of colorectal cancer at the age of 68
createdAt: 2026-07-27T00:00:00.000Z
slug: 20260727-01
published: true

# My Impression of Keigo Higashino
The first work by Keigo Higashino that I read was probably *The Miracles of the Namiya General Store*.

I remember it was when I was in elementary school. I was spending my summer vacation at my cousin’s house, and since there were no phones to play with back then, I had no choice but to read. As it happened, there was a copy of *The Miracles of the Namiya General Store* there. Judging solely by the title, I thought it would be a light, slice-of-life kind of book. It turned out to be quite fascinating. The redemption brought about through letters sent across time left a deep impression on me, and I remembered the author.

The next time I encountered his work was in my second year of high school.

At the time, people in our dormitory started passing around *Journey Under the Midnight Sun*. I remember that at least three of us read it on the same Kindle. We were genuinely so engrossed that we barely ate or slept—it was almost as intense as binge-watching *Breaking Bad*. BTW, even when I read online novels, I was never as enthusiastic as I was with this one. When it was my turn to read it, I would basically finish my homework as quickly as possible during self-study periods and then sneak a look, read while eating, and keep reading even after the dormitory lights had been turned off (thank goodness for this backlit Kindle). It was my first time reading a mystery novel with such mature subject matter. Although it was dark, it also had a certain sense of realism, and the way the main plot progressed through the alternating perspectives of the male and female leads was quite interesting. More importantly, the story was full of twists and turns, and it was very difficult to guess who the killer was. The most heartbreaking part was that Ryoji Kirihara ultimately protected Yukiho by taking his own life, only for Yukiho to say expressionlessly, “I don’t know this person at all.”

The next time I encountered “Yukiho” was in *The Phantom Night*. This story wasn’t as compelling as *Journey Under the Midnight Sun*, though it was still fairly decent. The ending of *The Phantom Night* was also very similar to that of *Journey Under the Midnight Sun*: the male protagonist eventually discovers that the female protagonist has been deceiving and using him all along, but in the end, he still takes his own life to protect her, allowing her to escape without suspicion.

I won’t go into all his other books one by one. The image below shows the works by Keigo Higashino that I’ve read.
![Works by Keigo Higashino that I’ve read|475](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/20260808043442545.png)


Keigo Higashino was a great writer. I’m grateful to him for enabling someone like me, who isn’t accustomed to reading, to concentrate and finish an entire book. I’m also grateful for the stories he created, which stay with you long after you’ve finished them.

R.I.P.

# 我對東野圭吾的印象
我第一次閱讀東野圭吾的作品，應該是他的《解憂雜貨店》。

我記得那時候還在國小，暑假在表姐家玩。那時沒有手機可以玩，於是只能看書了，剛好有一本《解憂雜貨店》。單從書名來看，我以為是日常休閒類型的書呢。這本書相當精彩，透過跨越時空的信件實現救贖，也讓我記住了這位作者。

下一次再相見就是高二了。

當時我們宿舍開始傳閱《白夜行》，我記得至少有三個人是用那台 Kindle 看完《白夜行》的。當時真的是廢寢忘食，跟追《絕命毒師》有得一比。順帶一提，我追網路小說都沒有追這本那麼積極。輪到我看的時候，我基本上就是自習課抓緊時間寫完作業後開始偷偷看、邊吃飯邊看，寢室熄燈了也繼續看（感謝這款有背光的 Kindle）。這是我第一次看這種尺度有點大的懸疑小說，雖然黑暗，卻又有一種真實感，而且男女雙視角的主線推進也滿有意思的。更重要的是，劇情確實相當跌宕起伏，凶手很難猜。最讓人意難平的是，桐原亮司最後透過自殺保護了雪穗，雪穗居然能面無表情地說出：「我完全不認識這個人。」

後來再次見到「雪穗」就是在《幻夜》中了。這個故事寫得沒有《白夜行》精彩，也算差強人意吧。《幻夜》的結局也和《白夜行》很像，男主角最後知道了女主角一直在欺騙和利用自己，但是最後他還是為了保護女主角而自殺，讓女主角清白脫身。

其他書就不一一贅述了，下面圖中是我看過的東野圭吾作品。
![看過的東野圭吾作品|475](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/20260808043442545.png)


東野圭吾是一位偉大的作家，感謝他讓我這個不習慣看書的人也能集中精神讀完一本完整的書，也感謝他創作的故事讓人回味無窮。

R.I.P.

---
title: Build a Personal Website with Cloudflare
description: "Architecture of this site: two Workers, one SQL database, and one object storage bucket"
createdAt: 2026-08-13T00:00:00.000Z
updatedAt: 2026-08-13T00:00:00.000Z
published: true
tags:
  - Network
  - Website building
  - Optimization
slug: 20260813-02
---

## Quotation

My website runs on two Cloudflare Workers, one SQL database, and one object storage service. Comments, likes, and page views are all updated in real time. My book, music, and movie collection has its own admin dashboard, and my music-listening rankings sync automatically every day in the early hours. Apart from the domain, the rest of the bill is essentially zero.

This article introduces its structure. It is currently made up of`muelsyse-blog`directly holds the blog domain; the other`blog-art-cover-fetcher`Responsible for fetching cover images and making them available to the application through a service binding. The admin path is protected by Cloudflare Access, and scheduled synchronization tasks also run in the application Worker.

![The Blog’s Cloudflare Architecture](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-cloudflare-architecture-e308f5492721.png)

*Figure 1: The application Worker directly serves the blog domain, while the cover-fetching Worker is invoked via a service binding; D1, R2, and the static asset service each handle their respective storage and distribution responsibilities.*

## Single Request Flow

![Blog Request Processing Flow](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-cloudflare-request-34513a050cca.png)

*Figure 2: Requests are routed to static asset serving or application logic based on resource type. Pages and APIs that need data then access D1, R2, or external services as required by the business logic.*

## Database Design

D1 is Cloudflare’s managed SQLite database, used to store structured data such as comments, likes, view counts, and metadata for book, music, and movie collections.

R2 handles image hosting for article content and any image assets that need to be hosted. The main reason for choosing it is that outbound traffic is free—traffic charges are the biggest concern for an image host. Stable, directly accessible upstream cover images retain their original URLs instead of being duplicated in R2. Collection metadata is managed by D1; references to illustrations in the article body are stored in Markdown, while mappings for derived images are maintained in the build manifest.

## Image Pipeline

When I write articles in Obsidian, the image-hosting plugin uploads each image directly to R2 the moment I paste it, leaving an online URL in the Markdown. The article body references the original image via its URL, so large images don’t have to be added to the Git history every time I write.

During the build, the script generates AVIF and WebP variants for body images that need optimization, with target widths of 640 / 1280 / 1920 pixels, while avoiding upscaling based on the original image dimensions. The variants are uploaded to R2, and the mappings are written to the manifest. During rendering, the URL in the Markdown remains unchanged, but the output HTML is complete.`<picture>`: The browser selects the smallest adequate file based on the viewport and pixel density. The first image in the body is loaded at high priority, while the rest are lazy-loaded. The original image URL is retained as a fallback.

## Small Money-Saving Strategy

> If your site is a purely static blog, Astro with static asset hosting is sufficient; you don’t need to run any application Worker code.

If you need comments, an admin panel, or scheduled tasks, D1 combined with an SSR Worker is a relatively low-cost solution.

### Worker
Requests for static assets neither execute code nor count toward Workers’ 100,000 free requests per day. CSS, JavaScript, fonts, and local images all fall into this category—they’re free and unlimited. What actually consumes the 100,000-request daily allowance are requests that require the application Worker code to run, such as dynamic HTML rendering and API calls.

So I route as many requests as possible through the static layer. Only paths that require dynamic processing are configured to go through a Worker first. This keeps request usage largely within the free tier.

### D1
Pay attention to the number of rows read by D1. The free tier allows 5 million rows per day, but it counts rows scanned, not rows returned. A query that returns 20 comments could count tens of thousands of rows if it scans the entire table without using an index. Creating indexes on commonly filtered fields and paginating lists can help you make the most of D1’s free quota.

###  Be mindful of the free-tier limits.
The “zero cost” claim here needs a caveat: excluding the domain, the bill is approximately zero as long as traffic and data usage remain within the free tiers. The specific quotas are (July 2026):

| Project              | Free allowance                  |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Workers dynamic requests | 100,000/day, shared across the account |
| Static asset requests | Free, unlimited                  |
| D1                   | 5 million row reads/day, 100,000 row writes/day |
| R2                   | 10 GB of storage, free egress   |

Note that 100,000 requests is the free daily limit for the entire account, not 100,000 per Worker. Full-table scans in D1 may quickly consume read quotas; whether charges are incurred also depends on the plan and usage. The quotas listed in the table reflect the information recorded at the time, so you should still verify the official pricing before enabling services or scaling up.

## Accelerated access in mainland China

Cloudflare’s default entry point is Anycast, with routing determined by BGP, which isn’t always ideal for China’s three major carriers. For the same site, China Telecom may be fast, while China Mobile may take a circuitous route and experience packet loss during the evening peak. My approach is to use an optimized CNAME: point the domain to a target domain that continuously measures performance and updates its DNS resolution results.

Once visitors reach the site, loading speed depends on layered caching, with the rules determined by how often the content changes:

- CSS / JS / fonts with content hashes: cache for one year
- HTML:`no-cache`, the cache must be revalidated before it can be reused
- Dynamic APIs such as comments and analytics: cache at the edge for 15 seconds; all write requests uniformly`no-store`.
- The GitHub contribution graph is cached for 6 hours, and WakaTime data is cached for 15 minutes.

## TL;DR

Serve static content directly wherever possible, put dynamic logic in the application Worker, and store structured data in D1 and article images in R2. First, clarify the routing and caching boundaries, then determine based on actual usage whether a paid plan is necessary.

## References

- [Workers Platform Limitations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/)
- [Static Asset Billing Rules](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/billing-and-limitations/)
- [Service Bindings](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/service-bindings/)
- [D1 Pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/pricing/)
- [R2 Pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/)
- [MDN: Cache-Control](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Cache-Control)

---
title: 基於 Cloudflare 建構個人網站
description: 此站架構介紹：兩個 Worker、一個 SQL 資料庫、一個物件儲存空間
createdAt: 2026-08-13T00:00:00.000Z
updatedAt: 2026-08-13T00:00:00.000Z
published: true
tags:
  - 網路
  - 建立網站
  - 最佳化
slug: 20260813-02
---

## 引文

我的這個網站運作著兩個 Cloudflare Worker、一個 SQL 資料庫和一個物件儲存。評論、按讚、瀏覽量都是即時的，書影音收藏有自己的管理後台，聽歌排行每天凌晨自動同步。而帳單上除了網域之外，其他部分的成本幾乎等於零。

這篇文章介紹它的架構。目前由`muelsyse-blog`直接持有部落格網域；另一個`blog-art-cover-fetcher`負責封面抓取，透過服務繫結供應用程式呼叫。後台路徑由 Cloudflare Access 保護，定時同步任務也在應用程式 Worker 中執行。

![部落格的 Cloudflare 架構](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-cloudflare-architecture-e308f5492721.png)

*圖 1：應用程式 Worker 直接承接部落格網域，封面抓取 Worker 透過服務繫結呼叫；D1、R2 與靜態資源服務各自負責儲存與分發。*

## 單一請求鏈路

![部落格請求處理流程](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-cloudflare-request-34513a050cca.png)

*圖 2：請求依資源類型進入靜態資源服務或應用程式邏輯。需要資料的頁面與 API 再依業務需求存取 D1、R2 或外部服務。*

## 資料庫設計

D1 是 Cloudflare 託管的 SQLite 資料庫，用來儲存結構化資料：留言、按讚、瀏覽次數、書籍、影音收藏的中繼資料等等。

R2 負責文章內文的圖床，以及需要託管的圖片資源。之所以選用它，主要是因為出口流量免費；對圖床來說，最怕的就是流量費。對於穩定且可直接連線的上游封面，則保留原始網址，不重複搬到 R2。收藏中繼資料由 D1 管理；內文插圖的引用保存在 Markdown 中，衍生圖片的對應關係則由建置清單維護。

## 圖片處理管線

我在 Obsidian 裡寫文章，貼上圖片的瞬間，圖床外掛就會直接將圖片上傳到 R2，Markdown 裡留下的是一個線上 URL。內文透過 URL 引用原圖，避免每次寫作都把大圖加入 Git 歷史紀錄。

建置時，腳本會為需要最佳化的正文圖片產生 AVIF 與 WebP 衍生圖，目標寬度包括 640／1280／1920 像素，並根據原圖尺寸避免放大。衍生圖會上傳至 R2，對應關係寫入 manifest。渲染時，Markdown 裡的那個 URL 不變，輸出的 HTML 卻是完整的`<picture>`：瀏覽器會根據視窗大小與像素密度，選擇最小但足夠的檔案；正文中的第一張圖片以高優先順序載入，其餘圖片則延遲載入。保留原圖 URL 作為備援。

## 省錢小策略

> 如果你的網站是純靜態部落格，使用 Astro 搭配靜態資源託管就夠了，不需要執行應用程式的 Worker 程式碼。  
如果需要留言、後台或排程工作，D1 搭配 SSR Worker 是一種成本較低的組合。

### Worker
命中靜態資源的請求不會執行程式碼，也不會計入 Workers 每天 10 萬次的免費請求額度。CSS、JS、字型、本地圖片都屬於這類資源，免費且不限量。真正會消耗每天 10 萬次免費額度的，是需要執行應用程式 Worker 程式碼的請求，例如動態 HTML 渲染和 API 呼叫。

所以我讓盡可能多的請求停留在靜態層，只有必須動態處理的路徑才設定為先經過 Worker。這樣一來，請求用量基本上都在免費額度範圍內。

### D1
留意 D1 的資料列讀取量。D1 每天提供 500 萬列的免費額度，但計算的是掃描列數，而不是回傳列數。一個回傳 20 則留言的查詢，如果沒有使用索引而掃描了整張資料表，計算的可能是幾萬列。為常用的篩選欄位建立索引，並對清單進行分頁，這些最佳化能最大限度地利用 D1 的免費額度。

###  注意免費額度限制
這裡所說的零成本需要加上限定條件：除了網域名稱之外，只要流量和資料量都在免費額度內，帳單就約等於零。具體額度如下（2026 年 7 月）：

| 項目           | 免費額度                   |
| -------------- | -------------------------- |
| Workers 動態請求 | 10 萬次／天，帳戶共用       |
| 靜態資源請求       | 免費，不限量             |
| D1           | 每天 500 萬行讀取，10 萬行寫入 |
| R2           | 10 GB 儲存空間，出口流量免費    |

注意，10 萬次是整個帳戶每天的免費上限，不是每個 Worker 各 10 萬次。D1 的全表掃描可能會迅速消耗讀取額度；是否產生費用還取決於方案和用量。表中的額度是當時的紀錄，啟用和擴充前仍要核對官方定價。

## 中國大陸存取加速

Cloudflare 的預設入口是 Anycast，路由由 BGP 決定，對中國大陸的三大電信業者不總是友善。同一個網站，電信可能很快，移動在晚間尖峰時段可能繞路並發生封包遺失。我的做法是使用優選 CNAME：將網域名稱 CNAME 到一個會持續測速、更新解析結果的目標網域名稱。

進站後的速度取決於快取分層，規則則依內容的變更頻率來設定：

- 含內容雜湊的 CSS／JS／字型：快取一年
- HTML：`no-cache`，重用快取前需要重新驗證
- 評論、統計這類動態 API：邊緣快取 15 秒，寫入請求一律`no-store`。
- GitHub 熱力圖快取 6 小時，WakaTime 快取 15 分鐘。

## 懶人包

靜態內容盡量直接回傳，動態邏輯放在應用程式 Worker；結構化資料交給 D1，內文圖片交給 R2。先釐清路由與快取的邊界，再根據實際用量判斷是否需要付費。

## 參考

- [Workers 平台限制](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/)
- [靜態資源計費規則](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/billing-and-limitations/)
- [服務繫結](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/service-bindings/)
- [D1 定價](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/pricing/)
- [R2 定價](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/)
- [MDN：Cache-Control](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Cache-Control)

---
title: Automate Blog Updates with GitHub Actions
createdAt: 2026-08-13T00:00:00.000Z
published: true
updatedAt: 2026-08-13T00:00:00.000Z
description: Automate blog checks, builds, and Cloudflare deployments with a GitHub Actions pipeline.
tags:
  - Automation
  - actions
  - Cloudflare
slug: 20260813-01
---

## Automated Pipeline Workflow

GitHub Actions handles all checks, asset processing, and deployment, automatically syncing everything to Cloudflare.

![GitHub Actions Deployment Pipeline for the Blog](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-actions-pipeline-b4436589c249.png)

*Figure 1: Testing, building, and deployment are executed in sequence; if a preceding step fails, deployment does not continue. The manifest generated during the build is written back to the repository by the Action after deployment.*

1. **Local Push**: Push Markdown content to a GitHub repository via Git.
2. **CI Trigger**: GitHub Actions Capture`master`of the branch`push`events or manual triggers, then start the build environment.
3. **Automation Workflow**: Install dependencies and run tests, then prepare the content, sync images and translations, validate the build, and package the SSR artifacts.
4. **CF Deployment**：Use Cloudflare Wrangler to update the production service.
5. **Write Back the Build Artifact Manifest**: Commit automatically generated changes—including the image manifest, content ID mappings, and translations—back to the repository.

## GitHub Actions Configuration

The workflow is placed in the repository root’s`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`The core steps are shown below; this repository also includes concurrency controls, build manifest write-back, and cleanup of previous deployments. Refer to this file for the complete configuration:

```yaml
name: Deploy to Cloudflare

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install Chrome for diagram rendering
        run: npx puppeteer browsers install chrome

      - name: Run checks
        run: npm test

      - name: Build and deploy
        run: npm run deploy
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
```

## 自動化流程

所有驗證、資源處理與部署都在 GitHub Actions 中完成，並自動同步至 Cloudflare。

![部落格的 GitHub Actions 部署流程](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-actions-pipeline-b4436589c249.png)

*圖 1：測試、建置與部署依序執行；前置步驟失敗後不會繼續部署。建置產生的清單會在部署後由 Action 回寫至儲存庫。*

1. **從本機推送**：透過 Git 將 Markdown 內容推送到 GitHub 儲存庫。
2. **CI 觸發**：GitHub Actions 捕獲`master`分支的`push`事件，或接受手動觸發，然後啟動建置環境。
3. **自動化處理**：安裝相依套件並執行測試，接著執行內容準備、圖片同步、翻譯同步、建置驗證及 SSR 產物打包。
4. **CF 部署**：呼叫 Cloudflare Wrangler，更新線上服務。
5. **回寫建置產物清單**：將圖片 manifest、內容 ID 對應和翻譯等自動產生的變更提交回儲存庫。

## GitHub Actions 設定

工作流程放在儲存庫根目錄的`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`。以下展示核心步驟；目前儲存庫還設定了併發控制、建置清單回寫以及歷史部署清理，完整設定請以該檔案為準：

```yaml
name: Deploy to Cloudflare

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install Chrome for diagram rendering
        run: npx puppeteer browsers install chrome

      - name: Run checks
        run: npm test

      - name: Build and deploy
        run: npm run deploy
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          OPENAI_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_BASE_URL }}
          API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ secrets.MODEL }}
          PUBLIC_BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
```

### 重要設定說明
在 GitHub 儲存庫設定中的`Secrets and variables -> Actions`新增`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`和`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`。本專案的建置還會呼叫翻譯服務，因此需要相應的`OPENAI_BASE_URL`、`API_KEY`和`MODEL`設定。金鑰只放在 Secrets 中。

`npm run deploy`會先執行建置；建置的前置腳本再依序準備內容、同步圖片和翻譯。清單回寫需要工作流程具有`contents: write`權限，提交訊息使用`[skip ci]`，避免提交建置產物時重複觸發部署。

---
title: Router Optimization Strategies for Environments with Multiple Competing APs
description: In competition environments such as Robocon, where interference is heavy and the network environment is complex, make appropriate trade-offs when selecting the router’s channel and channel width based on an on-site spectrum scan.
createdAt: 2026-10-23T00:00:00.000Z
tags:
  - Network
  - Router
  - Optimization
  - Get to the bottom of things
published: true
slug: 20261023-01
---

## Introduction

At robotics competitions such as Robocon, network conditions are often extremely complex.

At the time, my router was using the factory-default 80 MHz channel width, which happened to overlap with the most congested frequency band. WebRTC video streaming suffered severe stuttering, and latency at one point spiked to over one second.

A scan of the wireless environment at the venue found 88 Wi-Fi signals actively transmitting:

![Spectrum scan at the competition](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/20261025165234244.png)

The frequency scan results show that a large number of devices are clustered within the same channel and bandwidth ranges. Intuitively, it’s like having too many cars on the road: taking a less congested route might get you there faster. However, the scan list only shows which signals are nearby; it does not directly indicate channel utilization. I still need to switch the channel bandwidth and channel, then check whether the video latency improves.

Here, I’d like to analyze the causes of Wi-Fi lag from the perspective of radio principles, while also using this as notes for my own study of communications.

---

## Why Does Wi-Fi Stutter?

### 1. Channel Contention and Backoff (CSMA/CA)
Wi-Fi uses the half-duplex CSMA/CA mechanism. Before sending data, a device must perform carrier sensing.

Whether a channel is busy must be determined based on Wi‑Fi preamble detection, energy detection, and virtual carrier sensing; it cannot be characterized by a single fixed RSSI threshold. During contention, devices wait for the channel to become idle and perform random backoff. When many nearby devices are active, queuing, collisions, and retransmissions all increase latency and jitter.

### 2. Probability of Conflicts with Multiple Bound Channels
My router uses 80 MHz by default, formed by bonding four contiguous 20 MHz subchannels (see details in[Bandwidth and Channel Bonding](#频宽与信道绑定)). During on-site scanning, some hotspots are concentrated within similar channel ranges; the channels available to a hotspot also depend on the device and regional settings.

When transmitting over the full 80 MHz bandwidth, the protocol requires checking whether the primary and secondary channels are busy or idle. If the secondary channel is busy, devices that support dynamic bandwidth may switch to 40 MHz or 20 MHz transmission instead of waiting indefinitely.

For a simplified analysis, assume that each subchannel is occupied with the same probability $p$ and that the occupancy events are independent. Then, the probability that all four subchannels are idle simultaneously is $(1-p)^4$. In practice, occupancy is often correlated, and protocols also allow dynamic bandwidth reduction, so this equation only helps illustrate that wider channels are more likely to encounter occupancy; it cannot directly predict throughput in the field.

### 3. Strong Co-Channel Interference and Modulation Downgrade
The stronger the interference signals nearby, the lower the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (see [Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR)](#信干噪比-sinr)).

According to Shannon’s theorem (see [Shannon’s Theorem](#香农定理)), with the bandwidth unchanged, a lower $\text{SINR}$ corresponds to a lower theoretical capacity. Wi-Fi 6 can use higher-order modulation up to 1024-QAM, but this requires better signal quality; the specific threshold depends on the coding rate, receiver, and target packet error rate, and cannot be uniformly expressed as a fixed dB value (see[QAM Modulation](#qam-调制)).

When link quality deteriorates, rate control may select a lower modulation and coding scheme, while retransmissions may also increase, resulting in lower actual throughput.

---

## Solution: Balancing Channels and Bandwidth On-Site

### 1. Reduce Bandwidth to Improve the Baseline Resistance to Interference
Blindly choosing higher bandwidth in a high-interference environment can backfire. According to the thermal noise formula (see [Thermal Noise Floor Formula](#热噪声底噪公式)), increasing bandwidth from 20 MHz to 80 MHz physically raises the background noise floor by:

$$\Delta N = 10 \log_{10}(4) \approx 6 \text{ dB}$$

This compares the integrated thermal noise when the temperature and receiver conditions are the same and the total received signal power remains constant. An increase in noise power lowers the signal-to-noise ratio; if transmit power varies with bandwidth, the result will also differ. This does not mean that the modulation’s inherent signal-to-noise ratio threshold has been raised, nor does it by itself show that narrower bandwidth is necessarily faster.

### 2. Spectrum Scanning and Avoidance
In a complex network environment, first use a spectrum scanning tool to collect information about nearby signals:
- Received signal strength (RSSI)
- Operating channel
- Operating bandwidth

When selecting a channel, I first avoid APs with severe overlap and very strong received signals, then validate the choice through real-world load testing. RSSI strength cannot be directly equated with the other AP’s transmit power, nor is there a $-60 \text{ dBm}$ avoidance threshold that applies to every venue.

### 3. On-Site Tuning in Practice
An analysis of the scan results above shows that the default 80 MHz bandwidth range was heavily congested. By contrast, channel 165 and channels 52 through 64 were not only clear, but also free of high-power interference signals.

Channels 52–64 are subject to DFS (Dynamic Frequency Selection) requirements, meaning devices must detect and avoid radar in accordance with local regulations. Some devices do not make these channels available in hotspot mode, but scan results alone cannot establish that this is due to certification or legal restrictions. When selecting DFS channels, also consider the detection wait time, radar-triggered channel changes, and client compatibility.

With the configurations available on my equipment, channel 165 can operate at 20 MHz. It was relatively uncongested in the scan at the time, making it a candidate for sacrificing peak throughput in favor of stability, though this still needs to be validated on site.

At the time, I switched to channels 52 and 56, with the bandwidth set to 40 MHz. As soon as the change was complete, the WebRTC video stream returned to smooth playback, latency dropped to normal levels, and interruptions disappeared entirely.

---

## Appendix: Wi-Fi Fundamentals

### AP
AP stands for Access Point. It is the radio transmission hub that connects a wired local area network to wireless clients such as phones.

Home wireless routers typically integrate an AP transmitter, network routing, and switching functions.

### Frequency Bands
#### 2.4 GHz
- The frequency range is typically 2400 MHz to 2483.5 MHz.
- Lower frequency and longer wavelength provide better wall penetration, but transmission speeds are slower. Common devices include Bluetooth devices, wireless mice, and smart home devices.

#### 5 GHz
- The total available continuous spectrum spans several hundred MHz, with common bands covering 5150 to 5350 MHz and 5725 to 5850 MHz.
- Higher frequency and shorter wavelength mean greater attenuation through walls. The main advantage is very high transmission speed.

### Channel Allocation
Communication protocols divide continuous spectrum into discrete center frequencies at fixed intervals. Each designated frequency, along with the physical bandwidth it occupies, is collectively referred to as a channel.

In the common 5 GHz channel-planning scheme discussed here, every increase of 1 in the channel number corresponds to a 5 MHz increase in the center frequency; 20 MHz is a basic channel width, not the only channel width used by Wi-Fi.

To prevent adjacent channels from overlapping in the 5 GHz band, channel numbers must be separated by 4 (for example, 36, 40, 44, and 48; or 149, 153, 157, and 161).

### Bandwidth and Channel Bonding
Common Wi-Fi bandwidths include 20 MHz, 40 MHz, 80 MHz, and 160 MHz.

#### 20 MHz
Taking 802.11ac 20 MHz OFDM as an example, a 64-point FFT is used, with 52 subcarriers carrying data, along with pilot, DC, and guard subcarriers. The configuration varies across Wi-Fi generations and channel bandwidths.

#### 40 MHz / 80 MHz / 160 MHz
Wide channel bandwidth is achieved through channel bonding. Taking 80 MHz as an example, the RF and baseband layers combine four contiguous 20 MHz channels (such as 149, 153, 157, and 161) into a single channel at the underlying layer. Under the corresponding signal-to-noise ratio conditions, a wider bandwidth can provide higher theoretical capacity.

When bonding multiple channels, the router must designate one of them as the primary channel. Beacons and other frames used for discovery and compatibility are typically transmitted over the primary 20 MHz channel, allowing clients to establish a connection accordingly. The exact transmission method still depends on the frame type and protocol mode.

### Shannon’s Theorem

$$C = B \cdot \log_2 \left( 1 + \frac{S}{N + I} \right)$$

- $C$: Maximum channel transmission rate
- $B$: Physical bandwidth
- $S$: Received power of the useful signal
- $N$: Ambient background thermal noise
- $I$: Co-channel interference power

### Thermal Noise Floor Formula

$$N = k \cdot T \cdot B, \qquad N_{\mathrm{dBm}} = 10 \log_{10}\left(\frac{kTB}{1,\mathrm{mW}}\right)$$

- $k$: Boltzmann constant
- $T$: absolute temperature
- $B$: Receive bandwidth
- $N$: thermal noise power within this bandwidth, in watts; use the latter formula when converting to dBm.

Increase in the noise floor as bandwidth grows by a factor:

$$\Delta N = 10 \log_{10}\left(\frac{B_2}{B_1}\right)$$

At the same temperature and reception conditions, integrated thermal noise power increases by approximately $3\text{ dB}$ each time the bandwidth doubles; an actual receiver’s noise figure must also be taken into account.

### Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR)

- **SNR** (signal-to-noise ratio): $\text{SNR} = \frac{S}{N}$
- **SINR** (signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio): $\text{SINR} = \frac{S}{N + I}$

$$\mathrm{SINR}_{\mathrm{dB}} = 10\log_{10}\left(\frac{S}{N+\sum_i I_i}\right)$$

Power must first be summed in linear units; dBm values from multiple interference sources cannot be added directly. Only when a single co-channel interferer is dominant, thermal noise can be neglected, and both power levels are measured at the same receiving location and over the same bandwidth can the dBm difference between the desired signal and that interferer be used to estimate the SINR approximately. The RSSI values for individual APs listed by scanning tools do not directly provide the SINR during communication.

### QAM Modulation
Binary modulation carries 1 bit per symbol; higher-order modulation uses more distinguishable states to encode more bits in each symbol.

QAM uses in-phase and quadrature components to form a constellation diagram. The receiver recovers the information by distinguishing between constellation points; \(M\)-QAM maps at most \(\log_2 M\) bits per symbol. The effective data rate must also account for channel coding and protocol overhead.

| Modulation Scheme | Number of Bits Mapped to Each Subcarrier Symbol |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1024-QAM | 10 bits |
| 256-QAM | 8 bits |
| 64-QAM | 6 bits |
| 16-QAM | 4 bits |
| QPSK | 2 bits |

The higher the modulation order, the more densely packed the constellation points, and the greater the usual requirements for signal quality and receiver error performance. No universal SINR threshold is specified here: different coding rates, target packet error rates, and device implementations produce different results.

title: 使用 Cloudflare R2 + PicGo 實現免費圖床
description: 基於 Cloudflare R2 物件儲存與 PicGo 建構零出口流量費的圖床，實現 Obsidian 與 Typora 寫作時即時自動上傳。
tags:

  - 圖片託管服務
createdAt: 2026-10-25T00:00:00.000Z
published: true
slug: 20261025-01
---

## 方案架構

使用 Cloudflare R2 取代傳統物件儲存，作為圖床後端。

![PicGo 上傳到 R2 並回寫圖片連結](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-picgo-upload-5539b593dd45.png)

*圖 1：編輯器呼叫本機 PicGo，PicGo 上傳物件後依自訂網域產生公開 URL，再交由編輯器替換圖片引用。*

1. 編輯器貼上圖片會觸發本機 PicGo 上傳。
2. PicGo 透過 S3 相容 API 將圖片推送至 R2。
3. PicGo 外掛會根據設定的 Custom Domain 與物件路徑組合成公開連結，編輯器外掛再自動替換圖片網址。

---
## 為什麼選擇 Cloudflare R2

都免費給你用了，那還有什麼好說的呢？對我這種個人用的圖床來說，免費額度算是很充足，而且沒有出口流量費。不過，免費的是額度內的儲存空間和請求量，大量存取或頻繁上傳仍可能超出額度。中國大陸直連的速度也要看線路，不能只看帳單。

以下是撰寫時記錄的 Standard 儲存價格，實際開通前以[R2 官方定價](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/)為準：

| 資源項目                  | Cloudflare R2 每月免費額度 | 超額計費單價          |
| :-------------------- | :------------------ | :-------------- |
| **儲存空間**              | 10 GB / 月           | $0.015 / GB / 月 |
| **Class A 操作（寫入/列出）** | 100 萬次 / 月          | $4.50 / 百萬次     |
| **Class B 操作（讀取/下載）** | 1000 萬次 / 月         | $0.36 / 百萬次     |
| 出口流量                  | **出口流量不收費**        | **$0.00**       |

---
## Cloudflare R2 啟用與準備

### 先決條件
1. 登入 Cloudflare Dashboard，進入「R2 Object Storage」。
2. 綁定信用卡或 PayPal 完成帳戶驗證。在額度內不會產生費用。
> 沒有卡的話，可以去海鮮市場看看，10 RMB 以內就能搞定。

### 網頁手動設定
1. **建立 Bucket**：在 R2 頁面點選「Create bucket」，輸入名稱，Location 選 Automatic。
2. **綁定公開的 Custom Domain**：進入 Bucket ->「Settings」->「Public Access」-> 點選「Connect Domain」，輸入次網域（例如 `img.yourdomain.com`）。
3. **取得 API 憑證**：
   - **Account ID**：在 R2 概覽頁右下角的「Account Details」直接點擊複製。
   - **Access Key ID 與 Secret Access Key**：
	  1. 點選「Account Details」下方的「Manage API Tokens」進入權杖頁面。
	  2. 點選「Create Account API token」。
	  3. Permissions 選擇「Object Read & Write」，依需求指定 Bucket。
	  4. 點選建立，並在**最終成功頁面**立即複製並儲存 `Access Key ID` 與 `Secret Access Key`。

title: 多 AP 競爭環境下的路由器最佳化策略
description: 在 robocon 這類干擾眾多、網路環境複雜的比賽現場，根據現場頻譜掃描結果，妥善權衡路由器的頻道與頻寬
createdAt: 2026-10-23T00:00:00.000Z
tags:
  - 網路
  - 路由器
  - 最佳化
  - 打破砂鍋問到底
published: true
slug: 20261023-01
---

## 引言

在 Robocon 等機器人比賽現場，網路環境往往極度複雜。

我的路由器當時使用出廠預設的 80 MHz 頻寬，恰好落入最擁擠的頻段。當時 WebRTC 視訊串流嚴重卡頓，延遲一度飆升至 1 秒以上。

在現場使用工具掃描周遭無線環境，共發現 88 個正在發射的 Wi-Fi 訊號：

![比賽現場掃頻圖](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/20261025165234244.png)

從掃頻結果可以看出，大量裝置集中在相同的頻道與頻寬範圍內。直覺上，就像車多了容易塞車，換一條比較空的路可能更快。不過，掃描清單只顯示附近有哪些訊號，並不直接等同於頻道使用率；我還是得透過切換頻寬和頻道，再觀察視訊延遲是否有所改善。

這裡我想從無線電原理出發，分析 Wi-Fi 卡頓的原因，也算是自己學習通訊知識的筆記。

---

## 為什麼 Wi-Fi 會卡頓？

### 1. 頻道搶佔與退避機制（CSMA/CA）
Wi-Fi 採用半雙工的 CSMA/CA 機制。裝置傳送資料前必須進行載波偵聽。

頻道是否忙碌，必須結合 Wi‑Fi 前導碼偵測、能量偵測及虛擬載波感測來判斷，不能用單一固定的 RSSI 門檻概括。設備在競爭過程中會等待頻道空閒，並執行隨機退避；附近的活躍設備越多，排隊、碰撞和重傳就會增加延遲與抖動。

### 2. 多頻道綁定的機率衝突
我的路由器預設使用 80 MHz，由 4 個連續的 20 MHz 子頻道綁定而成（詳見[頻寬與頻道綁定](#频宽与信道绑定)）。現場掃描中，一些熱點集中在相近的頻道範圍內；熱點可選用的頻道還取決於裝置與地區設定。

使用完整的 80 MHz 頻寬傳送時，需要依照協定檢查主、次頻道的忙閒狀態。次頻道繁忙時，支援動態頻寬的裝置也可能改用 40 MHz 或 20 MHz 傳送，並非只能一直等待。

若僅作簡化分析，假設各子頻道以相同機率 $p$ 被佔用，且佔用事件彼此獨立，那麼四個子頻道同時閒置的機率是 $(1-p)^4$。實際上的佔用情況往往具有相關性，而協定又允許動態降低頻寬，因此這個式子只能幫助理解「較寬的頻道更容易遇到佔用」，不能直接預測現場吞吐量。

### 3. 同頻強干擾與調變回退
周圍干擾訊號強度越高，訊號干擾雜訊比越低（詳見 [訊號干擾雜訊比 SINR](#信干噪比-sinr)）。

根據香農公式（詳見 [香農定理](#香农定理)），在頻寬不變時，較低的 $\text{SINR}$ 對應較低的理論容量。Wi-Fi 6 的高階調變可以使用 1024-QAM，但它需要更好的訊號品質；具體門檻取決於編碼率、接收器和目標封包錯誤率，不能統一寫成某個固定的 dB 值（詳見[QAM 調變](#qam-调制)）。

當鏈路品質變差時，速率控制可能會選擇較低的調變編碼方案，重傳次數也會增加，因此實際吞吐量會下降。

---

## 解決方案：現場頻道與頻寬權衡

### 1. 降低頻寬，提升抗干擾能力
在高干擾環境下盲目選擇高頻寬會適得其反。根據熱雜訊公式（詳見 [熱雜訊底噪公式](#热噪声底噪公式)），頻寬從 20 MHz 增加到 80 MHz 時，背景底噪在物理上增加：

$$\Delta N = 10 \log_{10}(4) \approx 6 \text{ dB}$$

這裡比較的是在溫度與接收機條件相同、總接收訊號功率不變時的積分熱雜訊。雜訊功率增加會降低訊噪比；如果發射功率會隨頻寬變化，結果也會不同。這不代表調變本身的訊噪比門檻被提高，也不能單獨說明窄頻一定更快。

### 2. 頻譜掃描與避讓原則
在複雜網路環境下，首先使用掃頻工具採集周遭訊號狀態：
- 訊號接收強度（RSSI）
- 工作頻道
- 工作頻寬

選擇頻道時，我會先避開重疊嚴重、接收訊號很強的 AP，再結合實際負載測試。RSSI 強弱不能直接視為對方的發射功率，也沒有一條適用於所有現場的 $-60 \text{ dBm}$ 避讓線。

### 3. 現場調校實戰
分析前述掃頻結果，預設的 80 MHz 頻寬範圍重疊嚴重。相反地，頻道 165 以及頻道 52 至 64 不僅空曠，而且沒有高功率干擾訊號。

52 至 64 頻道涉及 DFS（Dynamic Frequency Selection，動態頻率選擇）要求，設備需要依所在地規定偵測並避讓雷達。部分設備的熱點模式不會開放這些頻道，但不能僅憑掃描結果斷定是認證或法律限制所致。選擇 DFS 頻道還要考慮等待偵測、雷達觸發切換頻道，以及終端相容性。

在我這套設備的可用設定中，信道 165 可按 20 MHz 運作。它在當時的掃描結果中相對空閒，可以作為犧牲峰值速率、換取穩定性的候選方案，仍需現場驗證。

當時現場選擇切換至頻道 52 與 56，對應頻寬設為 40 MHz。完成切換後，WebRTC 視訊串流立即恢復流暢，延遲降低至正常水準，斷流現象完全消除。

---

## 附錄：Wi-Fi 理論通識

### AP
AP（Access Point）的中文名稱是無線存取點。它是連接有線區域網路與無線終端（手機等）的射頻發射中樞。

家用無線路由器通常整合了 AP 發射、網路路由與交換器功能。

### 頻段
#### 2.4 GHz
- 頻率範圍通常為 2400 MHz 至 2483.5 MHz。
- 頻率低、波長長、穿牆能力強，但傳輸速度較慢。常用裝置包括藍牙、無線滑鼠及智慧家庭終端裝置。

#### 5 GHz
- 總可用連續頻譜達數百 MHz，常見頻段涵蓋 5150 至 5350 MHz 與 5725 至 5850 MHz。
- 頻率高、波長短、穿牆衰減大，主要優勢是傳輸速率極快。

### 頻道劃分
通訊協定在連續頻譜上按照固定步長劃分離散的中心頻率點，各個標定頻率及其所佔用的實體頻寬統稱為頻道。

在這裡討論的常見 5 GHz 頻道規劃中，頻道編號每增加 1，對應的中心頻率增加 5 MHz；20 MHz 是一種基本頻道寬度，並非 Wi-Fi 唯一的頻道寬度。

為了在 5 GHz 頻段內實現相鄰頻道互不重疊，頻道號碼之間需相隔 4 個單位（如 36、40、44、48 與 149、153、157、161）。

### 頻寬與頻道綁定
常見 Wi-Fi 頻寬包含 20 MHz、40 MHz、80 MHz 與 160 MHz。

#### 20 MHz
以 802.11ac 的 20 MHz OFDM 為例，使用 64 點 FFT，其中 52 個子載波承載資料，另外還有導頻、直流與保護子載波。不同世代與頻寬的配置各不相同。

#### 40 MHz / 80 MHz / 160 MHz
高頻寬採用頻道綁定機制。以 80 MHz 為例，射頻與基頻會在底層將 4 個連續的 20 MHz 頻道（如 149、153、157、161）拼接在一起。在相應的訊噪比條件下，更大的頻寬可以提供更高的理論容量。

綁定多個頻道時，路由器必須指定其中一個頻道作為主頻道。信標等用於探索與相容的訊框通常會透過主 20 MHz 頻道傳送，終端裝置據此建立連線；實際的傳送方式仍取決於訊框類型與通訊協定模式。

### 香農定理

$$C = B \cdot \log_2 \left( 1 + \frac{S}{N + I} \right)$$

- $C$：頻道極限傳輸速率
- $B$：實體頻寬
- $S$：接收有用訊號功率
- $N$：環境背景熱雜訊
- $I$：同頻干擾功率

### 熱雜訊底噪公式

$$N = k \cdot T \cdot B, \qquad N_{\mathrm{dBm}} = 10 \log_{10}\left(\frac{kTB}{1,\mathrm{mW}}\right)$$

- $k$：波茲曼常數
- $T$：絕對溫度
- $B$：接收頻寬
- $N$：該頻寬內的熱雜訊功率，單位為瓦；換算為 dBm 時使用後一個公式

頻寬成倍增加時的底噪升幅：

$$\Delta N = 10 \log_{10}\left(\frac{B_2}{B_1}\right)$$

在溫度與接收條件相同的情況下，積分熱雜訊功率會隨頻寬每翻倍增加約 $3\text{ dB}$；實際接收機還需計入雜訊指數。

### 訊號干擾雜訊比 SINR

- **SNR**（訊噪比）： $\text{SNR} = \frac{S}{N}$
- **SINR**（訊號干擾雜訊比）：$\text{SINR} = \frac{S}{N + I}$

$$\mathrm{SINR}_{\mathrm{dB}} = 10\log_{10}\left(\frac{S}{N+\sum_i I_i}\right)$$

功率需先以線性單位求和，不能直接將多個干擾源的 dBm 值相加。只有在某個同頻道干擾源占主導、可忽略熱雜訊，且兩項功率是在相同接收位置與頻寬下測得時，才能近似以有用訊號與該干擾源之間的 dBm 差值進行估算。掃描工具列出的各 AP RSSI 並不會直接給出通訊期間的 SINR。

### QAM 調變
二進位調變每個符號承載 1 bit；更高階的調變使用更多可區分的狀態，在每個符號中編碼更多 bit。

QAM 使用同相與正交兩個分量構成星座圖。接收端透過判別星座點來還原資訊；$M$-QAM 每個符號最多可映射 $\log_2 M$ 個位元。有效資料速率還要扣除通道編碼與通訊協定的額外負荷。

| 調變方式 | 每個子載波符號映射的位元數 |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1024-QAM | 10 位元 |
| 256-QAM | 8 位元 |
| 64-QAM | 6 位元 |
| 16-QAM | 4 位元 |
| QPSK | 2 位元 |

階數越高，星座點越密，對訊號品質和接收機誤差的要求通常越高。這裡不列出統一的 SINR 門檻：不同的編碼率、誤包率目標與設備實作會得到不同結果。

## Solution Architecture

Use Cloudflare R2 instead of traditional object storage as the image hosting backend.

![Upload images to R2 with PicGo and write back the image links](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-picgo-upload-5539b593dd45.png)

*Figure 1: The editor invokes the local PicGo. After uploading the object, PicGo generates a public URL using the custom domain and passes it back to the editor to replace the image reference.*

1. Pasting an image into the editor triggers an upload via the local PicGo app.
2. PicGo uploads images to R2 via its S3-compatible API.
3. The PicGo plugin constructs a public URL by combining the configured Custom Domain with the object path, and the editor plugin then automatically replaces the image URL.

---
## Why Choose Cloudflare R2

They’re practically giving it away for free—what more is there to say? For a personal image-hosting service like mine, the free allowance is fairly generous, and there are no egress traffic fees. That said, the free tier only covers storage and requests within the quota; lots of traffic or frequent uploads can still push you over the limit. Speeds for direct connections from mainland China also depend on the network route, so you can’t judge it by the bill alone.

The following are the Standard storage prices recorded at the time of writing; before activating it, refer to[Official R2 Pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/)shall prevail:

| Resource              | Cloudflare R2 Free Monthly Allowance | Overage Unit Price |
| :-------------------- | :------------------ | :-------------- |
|**Storage Space**| 10 GB / month           | $0.015 / GB / month |**Class A operations (write/list)**| 1 million requests / month | $4.50 / million requests     |
|**Class B operations (read/download)**| 10 million requests / month | $0.36 / million requests |
| Egress traffic                  |**No egress fees**|**$0.00**|

---
## Enabling and Preparing Cloudflare R2

### Prerequisites
1. Log in to the Cloudflare Dashboard and go to “R2 Object Storage.”
2. Link a credit card or PayPal account to verify your account. You won’t be charged as long as you stay within the usage limits.
> If you don’t have a card, you can check out the second-hand market—one for under RMB 10 will do the job.

### Manual Configuration via the Web Interface
1. **Create a Bucket**：On the R2 page, click “Create bucket,” enter a name, and set Location to “Automatic.”
2. **Bind a public Custom Domain**: Go to Bucket -> “Settings” -> “Public Access” -> click “Connect Domain” and enter a subdomain (e.g.`img.yourdomain.com`).
3. **Obtain API credentials**:
   - **Account ID**: On the bottom right of the R2 Overview page, click “Copy” in the “Account Details” section.
   - **Access Key ID and Secret Access Key**:
	  1. Click “Manage API Tokens” under “Account Details” to open the API token page.
	  2. Click “Create Account API Token.”
	  3. Select “Object Read & Write” under Permissions, and specify the Bucket as needed.
	  4. Click Create, and in**Final Success Page**Copy and save now`Access Key ID`and`Secret Access Key`.
  > **Note**:`Secret Access Key`The secret is displayed only once after successful generation. If you did not save the secret for a previously created token, you cannot view it again; click “Create Account API token” again to generate a new one.

### Agent
Operations such as creating a bucket can be completed by the agent via the Wrangler CLI. First, log in to your Cloudflare account, then verify that you have the permissions required for the specific operations. Custom domain configuration can also be handled through the Dashboard or the Cloudflare API. The Wrangler login session and the S3 access keys required by PicGo are separate sets of credentials and cannot be used interchangeably.

## PicGo Client Configuration

### 1. Install the Plugin
1. Open PicGo and go to “Plugin Settings.”
2. Search for and install`picgo-plugin-cloudflare-r2`.

### 2. Configure Parameters
Go to “Image Hosting Settings” → “Cloudflare R2” and fill in the following configuration fields:

|**Account ID**| View in the bottom-right corner of the R2 overview page      |
| :------------------ | :--------------- |
|**Access Key ID**| Access Key ID generated when creating the R2 token |
|**SecretAccessKey**| Secret Access Key generated at the same time |
|**Bucket name**| Created R2 Bucket    |
|**Storage path (optional)**| Specify directory levels as needed         |
|**Custom Domain**| R2 Custom Domain |

---

## Automatic, seamless uploads from the editor

### Obsidian Configuration
Use local PicGo to automatically upload pasted images to the image host and replace them:
1. Make sure PicGo is running.
2. Install in Obsidian`Image auto upload Plugin`Plugin.
3. Configure the plugin to use PicGo for image uploads.
4. Paste or drag images directly into your notes, and they’ll be uploaded to the R2 image host, with their local paths in the body text automatically replaced by remote image-host links.

### Typora Configuration
Configure it as shown in the diagram, then click “Verify image upload option” to test it.

![image.png](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/20261025185635532.png)

---

## Cache Optimization and Anti-Abuse Strategies

Although R2 offers free egress traffic, more than 10 million Class B read requests per month will still incur a small charge. Enabling CDN edge caching and protection is recommended.

In the Cloudflare Dashboard, go to the domain’s “Caching” → “Cache Rules” and add a rule:
- **Matching conditions**:`Hostname equals img.yourdomain.com`
- **Edge Cache TTL**: Replace the origin server and set it to 1 year (31536000 seconds)
- **Browser Cache TTL**: Set to 1 year

Requests served from the CDN cache do not need to read from R2 again, which reduces Class B operations. However, the request still goes back to the origin on the first visit, after the cache expires, or when the object is evicted from a cache node, so a long TTL cannot guarantee zero read charges. When browser caching is set to one year, use a new object name when updating an image to prevent readers from continuing to see the old version.

description: A deep-dive debugging story about a depth camera stream dropping out
title: ROS 2 Cyclone DDS Multicast Causes Camera Depth Stream Dropouts
published: true
tags:

slug: 20261021-01

## Case Review

### Background

Allow me to introduce the two suspects:

- MID-360 LiDAR | Wired Ethernet port, negotiated link speed of 100 Mbps
- Intel RealSense D435if depth camera | USB 3.0

In an earlier ROS 2 Humble project, I ran into intermittent failures where Actions and Services wouldn’t respond: the task state machine couldn’t get a Goal Handle, and the competition process would grind to a halt. To work around this, I switched ROS 2’s DDS middleware from the default Fast DDS to Cyclone DDS. I also compiled the camera driver and YOLO inference nodes as ROS 2 Components and loaded them into the same component container process to reduce the overhead of moving images around.

### The Trouble Begins

Everything had been working fine in testing, and I’d even finished the first version the day before we left. Based on our test results, we thought we had a real shot at first place nationally. We were already celebrating, thinking we’d finally broken the curse of always finishing projects right up against the deadline. Unfortunately, we celebrated too soon. Trouble was still on its way.

The workflow was nearly optimized, so I decided to make a change to our competition debugging tool. To make it easier to view the camera feed on-site, I overhauled the video streaming component in a web-based debugging page I’d built earlier. It was a bit like RViz. To keep latency low and control the bitrate, I chose WebRTC: a standalone Server node on the ROS 2 side subscribed to the camera’s RGB and depth images, encoded the frames for display as H.264, and sent them to my computer over WebRTC. In isolation, it worked as expected. But the problem was hiding in the word “standalone”: I’d added a cross-process subscriber outside the Component container. The local path from the camera to YOLO was still there, but the publisher now also had to deliver raw images to this new process over DDS. Since WebRTC compression only happened after the images arrived, it couldn’t help with that earlier transfer.

### DEBUG

Four hours before we were due to leave, all the trouble we’d set ourselves up for came to a head. After finishing the debugging tool, I was ready to run through the whole workflow again. The car moved, but it couldn’t recognize a single target. I checked the logs and saw that the YOLO inference node hadn’t even started inferring properly.

“Okay, let’s restart the process. There’s probably a 90% chance that’ll fix it.”

Nope. Still broken.

“Fine, I’ll ask AI.”

The AI looked at the logs and said the depth data had appeared briefly before dropping out, suggesting that the camera cable was loose. I breathed a sigh of relief. A loose cable was easy to fix—all I had to do was unplug it and plug it back in. Nope. Still no luck. I tried another cable, another USB port, and even another Thunderbolt port, but nothing worked. I also tried gemini-3.8-flash, gpt-6.1-sol, and gpt-6-astra one after another. None of them spotted the problem; instead, they started making random changes to the existing code, and at one point even the RGB feed disappeared.

With only an hour left before we had to leave and the problem still unsolved, I had no choice but to `git reset` back to the code that had worked the day before. I thought that if the old version ran, it would prove the hardware was fine. But it still wouldn’t run. I found out later that the WebRTC companion node was in a different workspace, so rolling back hadn’t touched it at all. At the time, though, I didn’t know that. I really thought the sky was falling. A software problem might still be fixable; if the hardware was broken, we were out of luck. There wasn’t a second camera to try, so all we could do was start packing. “Come on, let’s go. Here we are again: ‘Teacher, we have a video of it working.’”

I was exhausted on the way to the airport, but couldn’t sleep. The elevated highway was eerily empty at five in the morning. Streetlights stretched into a line through the pre-dawn darkness. Nobody spoke, and there was no car left to tinker with. I could only sit there, unable to touch anything or change anything. The frantic anxiety that had nearly driven me mad in those last few hours before we left slowly began to fade in the silence. I’d been rushing to put out the fire by restarting things, swapping cables, and asking AI for help, hoping to get lucky and fix it in the next second, but I hadn’t even done the basic work of changing one variable at a time.

“I can’t keep relying on that dumb lucky AI.” First, I needed to check RGB and depth separately in `realsense-viewer` and rule out ROS.

When we reached the gate, boarding was still half an hour away. I hurriedly connected the battery to the car to test it, and finally got some good news: when I viewed the camera on its own, both RGB and depth worked normally. That meant the hardware was fine. It was a software problem, so there was still hope.

At the hotel, the room was too cramped to run the whole workflow, so I started only the camera and inference nodes. I left the LiDAR and lower-level controller off. Huh—the camera was working normally, with both depth and RGB coming through. I still hadn’t realized that the LiDAR was the difference, since it had always been on during our pre-departure testing. So I celebrated too early again, thinking it must be some kind of mysterious fluke. Since it was working, I decided not to touch anything and got some sleep before the on-site debugging session that afternoon.

But as soon as we ran the full workflow at the venue, the camera went down again, and the depth stream dropped out as before. That’s when I remembered that I hadn’t turned on the LiDAR or the lower-level controller at lunchtime. I compared things one by one, and finally narrowed it down: whenever the LiDAR was powered on and connected to the mini PC, the camera’s depth stream would drop out. I told gemini-3.8-flash what I’d found, and Gemini went into panic mode again, suggesting that the LiDAR’s infrared light might be interfering with the camera. I thought it was possible: we had changed the arm’s initial position that day, so the LiDAR might have been scanning the camera. The D435 series uses active stereo depth and also has an infrared projector, so optical interference was worth checking. We raised the camera and tested again with the LiDAR covered by hand, but the stream still dropped out. It wasn’t until I asked gpt-6.1-sol to analyze the logs that we finally started looking at the network: even though the camera was connected over USB, that didn’t mean ROS image data traveled only over USB. The raw cross-process image traffic could be passing through the LiDAR’s 100 Mbps wired interface. After we restricted DDS’s user-data multicast, depth came back and the network port’s transmit rate dropped significantly. That finally pinned the problem on the communication configuration.

## Root Cause and How the Data Travels

### Analysis

The strongest evidence on-site was the link between the failure, the wired interface, and the DDS multicast policy: the stream dropped out when the LiDAR network was connected, recovered after setting `AllowMulticast` to `spdp`, and the physical interface’s transmit rate fell from around 100 Mbps to 0.003 Mbps. This supports the explanation that **high-bandwidth image data was being sent as DDS data multicast over the 100 Mbps link, causing network congestion**.

I didn’t run into a problem immediately after switching to Cyclone DDS because the communication topology was relatively simple at the time: the camera and YOLO were in the same container process, and with the right configuration they could communicate in-process. Later, when I added the WebRTC node in a separate process, it needed to receive raw images through RMW/DDS, adding another high-bandwidth transfer path. (The original in-process path wasn’t disabled.) Cyclone DDS chooses network paths based on interface capabilities, configuration, and discovered peers. In the on-site logs, the wireless interface showed `presumed flaky multicast, use for SPDP only`, while the wired interface showed `presumed robust multicast support, use for everything`. This reflects its default assessment of multicast support on each interface: wireless interfaces tend to be used only for discovery multicast, while wired interfaces may be used more broadly. It does not mean that “all wired interfaces will carry all traffic.” The actual choice also depends on the version, configuration, and subscription topology. The problem was that an interface allowed to carry data multicast doesn’t necessarily have enough bandwidth. A 1280 × 720 RGB8 image published at 30 Hz has a pixel payload of about 664 Mbps alone—far beyond the capacity of this 100 Mbps link, so it was bound to get stuck.

![ROS 2 Image Communication on the Same Host and Multicast Policies](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-ros-data-path-4c6bb401b377.png)

*Figure 2: An external subscriber adds a DDS image transfer path. After switching to `spdp`, multicast is used only for participant discovery, while endpoint matching and image transfer use unicast. Same-host destination addresses are usually delivered via local routing; remote subscribers still require the physical network.*

> Here’s another counterintuitive point: if the data has already arrived at the same computer over USB, why would it affect the physical network port? Because cross-process communication doesn’t automatically mean shared-memory communication. The DDS network path used here serializes the images and sends them through the UDP/IP stack. Unicast to a local address is usually delivered via local routing on Linux; data multicast can generate both traffic on a physical interface and local loopback delivery.

## Solution

The fix that worked was to restrict Cyclone DDS multicast to the participant discovery stage, so that endpoint matching and user data use unicast. Set this in the terminal where you start the ROS nodes:

```bash
export CYCLONEDDS_URI='<CycloneDDS><Domain Id="any"><General><AllowMulticast>spdp</AllowMulticast></General></Domain></CycloneDDS>'
```

You can also add it to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`, then reload the configuration before starting the relevant nodes. Already-running processes won’t automatically pick up the new environment variable, so they need to be restarted. If the nodes are managed by systemd, a container, or another launcher, pass the variable through that launch environment as well.

`AllowMulticast` values

| Value   | Behavior and notes |
| :------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `true`  | Allows multicast for discovery and user data; whether it is actually used also depends on the interfaces and peers. On bandwidth-constrained networks, check the transfer paths for high-bandwidth topics such as images. |
| `false` | Disables the multicast controlled by this setting. The default multicast discovery path is unavailable, but contact can be established through unicast discovery configuration such as `Peers`; this does not mean that “discovery for all nodes stops working entirely.” |
| `spdp`  | Keeps multicast only for SPDP participant discovery; endpoint matching and user data use unicast. In this case, it preserved convenient node discovery while avoiding image data multicast over the 100 Mbps interface. |

## Appendix

### Theoretical Calculations

#### Image Payload and 100 Mbps Bandwidth Limit

A useful clue at the time was that the RGB receive rate was only about 4.4 Hz. Working backward from the size of a single frame, its payload throughput was already close to 100 Mbps. The physical network port had also negotiated a rate of exactly 100 Mbps. This was consistent with the link being the bottleneck, though the calculation alone cannot replace packet capture or interface counters.

| Image stream | Resolution | Pixel encoding | Data per frame | Theoretical bandwidth at 30 Hz |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| RGB | 1280 × 720 | RGB8 (3 B/pixel) | 2.76 MB | **663.55 Mbps** |
| Native depth | 848 × 480 | Z16 / 16UC1 (2 B/pixel) | 0.81 MB | **195.38 Mbps** |
| Aligned depth | 1280 × 720 | 16UC1 (2 B/pixel) | 1.84 MB | **442.37 Mbps** |

The mini PC’s network port and the LiDAR had negotiated an actual link speed of **100 Mbps full duplex**. Full duplex means that data can be transmitted in both directions at the same time; it does not raise the limit in one direction to 200 Mbps. In the ideal case, without accounting for any protocol overhead, the maximum it can handle in one direction is:

$$100,000,000 \text{ bps} \div (1280 \times 720 \times 3 \times 8 \text{ bits}) \approx 4.52 \text{ fps}$$

The RGB receive rate on-site was **4.4 Hz**, equivalent to a pixel payload of about **97.3 Mbps**, close to this theoretical limit.

#### Comparison with Measured Data

| Metric | Before fix | After fix |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **Color image update rate** | 4.4 Hz | 13.9 Hz |
| **Native depth update rate** | 0 Hz | 29.7 Hz |
| **Aligned depth update rate** | 0 Hz | 14.2 Hz |
| **RGBD heartbeat rate** | 0 Hz | 14.1 Hz |
| **Median color image receive latency** | 943.9 ms | 58.3 ms |
| **Median native depth receive latency** | N/A | 42.1 ms |
| **Physical wired port transmit rate** | About 100 Mbps | **0.003 Mbps** |

Restoring communication doesn’t mean every stream is running at 30 Hz: native depth recovered to 29.7 Hz, but RGB, aligned depth, and the RGBD heartbeat were still around 14 Hz. This shows that the dropouts were alleviated; it doesn’t prove that the entire vision processing pipeline is free of other bottlenecks.

### Introduction to DDS

![ROS 2 Communication Layers and the In-Process Path](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-ros-layers-24212fd3eca3.png)

*Figure 5: The ROS 2 communication layers: client library, RMW, and DDS. An eligible in-process path can bypass DDS serialization; whether cross-process communication uses the network or shared memory depends on the implementation and configuration.*

DDS (Data Distribution Service) is a distributed data communication standard published by the OMG. ROS 2 typically relies on DDS for capabilities such as discovery, publish-subscribe, and QoS, organizing communication through Topics and data types. It uses **RMW (ROS Middleware Interface)** to separate the client API from the specific middleware implementation, allowing implementations to be switched within the limits of the supported interface. Unlike the centralized Master-based discovery commonly used in ROS 1, DDS can establish endpoint connections through distributed discovery. (However, the ROS 1 Master is not a relay for all user data either: after nodes establish a connection, user data is usually transferred directly, so a Master failure should not be equated with all existing data connections immediately dropping.) DDS implementations often interoperate through RTPS. UDP/IP is a common transport, but the DDS standard does not permit only this one transport.

### Fast DDS vs Cyclone DDS

The table below covers only the differences relevant to this issue; it does not attempt to assign absolute use cases to the two implementations based on this one on-site experience.

| Evaluation area | Fast DDS | Cyclone DDS |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Shared memory | Supports mechanisms such as shared-memory transport and data sharing. Whether they are enabled, or reduce serialization or copying, depends on the version, configuration, and message conditions. | Support depends on the version, build, and configuration; this article does not assume that “same-host communication” means shared memory is enabled. |
| Network interfaces and multicast | Network transport, discovery, and multicast behavior can be configured; check which configuration is actually in effect. | Offers interface selection and multicast policy configuration; this time, `AllowMulticast=spdp` avoided user-data multicast. |
| Behavior observed in this project | We had previously encountered unresponsive Actions / Services, but didn’t retain enough information to confirm the specific mechanism. | Dropouts occurred after adding an external image subscriber and a 100 Mbps wired interface; they stopped after restricting user-data multicast. |
| Selection and validation | Validate functionality, QoS, load, and fault recovery on the specific version in use. | Likewise, validate with the full node topology and actual network conditions; testing a single node isn’t enough. |

### ROS 2 Components

ROS 2 Components compile node implementations into dynamically loadable libraries, which a component container loads into the same process. This gives them a shared address space, making it easier to organize nodes and creating opportunities to reduce image copying. However, how the container schedules callbacks also depends on the executor, so it’s not always accurate to say that components “share one thread pool.” Nodes that continuously process large messages—such as camera publishers, image preprocessing, and YOLO inference—are good candidates for checking whether they can be placed in the same container. However, **componentization and in-process communication are two related but distinct configuration points**. In addition to placing the nodes together, you also need to enable `use_intra_process_comms` for the relevant nodes and confirm that the messages and QoS support this path.

#### How Componentization Can Improve Performance

When the conditions for in-process communication are met, messages can be delivered to local subscribers by transferring ownership of or sharing C++ objects, reducing two kinds of overhead:

1. **Message copying**: With compatible publisher and subscriber interfaces, a `std::unique_ptr` or a shared read-only message can be transferred. Whether copying is still required depends on the number of subscribers, callback signatures, and buffering strategy.
2. **Serialization**: Local in-process delivery can bypass DDS serialization and deserialization. If there are external subscribers too, the publisher still needs to prepare a middleware message for the external path.

So, “turn on Components and you get completely zero-copy” is not true. To verify the actual effect, you can use the ROS 2 in-process communication example to check message addresses, then measure CPU usage, memory bandwidth, and end-to-end latency under a real workload.

### Unicast

Unicast sends data to a specific destination address. In the same-host scenario described here, data sent to a local address can usually be delivered via local routing, while data sent to a remote host still needs the physical link. In this case, the benefit came from preventing high-bandwidth user-data multicast from entering a constrained interface.

### Multicast

IPv4 multicast uses addresses in the `224.0.0.0` to `239.255.255.255` range. A sender transmits data to a multicast group, and network devices handle it according to their multicast forwarding configuration. Receivers get the data by joining the multicast group. Whether a switch forwards traffic only to ports with members also depends on features such as IGMP snooping. If these features aren’t enabled or are misconfigured, traffic may be flooded to more ports. Multicast is useful for one-to-many transmission, but it is still constrained by link bandwidth, wireless conditions, and endpoint implementations.

容我介紹一下這兩位犯罪嫌疑人：

- MID-360 雷射雷達｜有線網路埠，實際協商速率 100 Mbps
- Intel RealSense D435if 深度攝影機｜USB 3.0

之前在 ROS 2 Humble 的專案裡，我遇到了 Action 與 Service 偶發沒有回應的問題：任務狀態機拿不到 Goal Handle，比賽流程就卡住了。為了繞開這個問題，我把 ROS 2 的通訊中介軟體 DDS 從預設的 Fast DDS 換成了 Cyclone DDS；同時，為了減少影像搬運的開銷，我還將相機驅動節點與 YOLO 推論節點編譯為 ROS 2 元件，載入到同一個元件容器行程中。

### 東窗事發

原本一直測試都沒問題，甚至在出發前一天就調好第一版了。照當時的測試成績，我們覺得進國一很有希望。大家都開香檳了，以為終於打破了做專案總要到 DDL 極限才調完的詛咒。可惜高興得太早，該來的還是要來。

流程已經最佳化得差不多了，我就想著改一下比賽除錯工具。為了在現場更直觀地看到相機畫面，我大幅改寫了之前做的一個 Web 除錯網頁中的影片串流元件，功能有點像 RViz。為了實現低延遲並控制位元率，我選擇了 WebRTC：ROS 2 端執行一個獨立的伺服器節點，訂閱相機的 RGB 與深度影像，將用於顯示的畫面編碼為 H.264 後，再透過 WebRTC 傳送到我的電腦。單獨測試時，效果符合預期，但問題恰恰就藏在這個「獨立」裡——我在元件容器外面增加了一個跨行程訂閱者。相機到 YOLO 的本機路徑雖然還在，發布者卻得額外透過 DDS 將原始影像交付給這個新行程，而 WebRTC 的壓縮發生在收到影像之後，救不了前面的這段傳輸。

### DEBUG

出發前的 4 個小時，埋下的雷集中爆發了。除錯工具完善後，我準備再跑一遍完整流程，結果車能動，目標卻一個也沒辨識出來，一看日誌，YOLO 推論節點壓根沒有正常開始推論。「好嘛，重啟一下行程，應該有 90% 的機率能解決吧。」壞了，沒解決。「那我就 AI 啟動吧。」AI 看了日誌，說是深度資料短暫出現後又斷開，推測相機線鬆了。我鬆了一口氣，線鬆了好辦啊，重新插拔一下不就行了。壞了，還是不行，換線、換 USB 連接埠、換 Thunderbolt 連接埠一輪試下來都沒用。我又輪番試了 `gemini-3.8-flash`、`gpt-6.1-sol`、`gpt-6-astra`，當時它們都沒有抓到問題，反而亂改現有程式碼，一度連 RGB 都沒了。

眼看離出發只剩一個小時，問題依然沒解決，最後只能 `git reset` 退回昨天跑通的程式碼。我想，只要舊版本能跑，就能說明這套硬體沒有壞，結果居然還是沒跑通——後來才知道，WebRTC 配套節點放在另一個工作區，這次回退根本沒動到它。但當時我不知道，真的覺得天塌了。軟體問題還有救，硬體壞了就真的沒轍，這會兒也找不出第二台相機，只能開始收拾東西，走吧走吧，又回到了那句「老師，我們有跑通的影片」。

去機場的路上，我很睏，卻睡不著。凌晨五點的高架空曠得出奇，路燈在破曉前的夜色裡連成一線，沒有人說話，也沒有能繼續除錯的車，我只能坐著，什麼也碰不到，什麼也改不了。出發前那幾個小時幾乎把人逼瘋的焦躁，反而在這陣沉默裡慢慢消退了。剛才一直急著靠重啟、換線、求助 AI 碰運氣，想在下一秒就把火撲滅，卻連最基本的控制變數都沒做好。「不能再依賴那個傻福 AI 了。」我得先用 `realsense-viewer` 單獨查看 RGB 和深度，把 ROS 的影響排除掉。

抵達登機門時，離登機還有半小時。我趕忙替車裝上電池測試，終於拿到一個好消息：單獨查看相機時，RGB 和深度都正常。說明硬體是沒毛病的，是軟體問題，還有救。

到了飯店，房間太窄，沒辦法跑完整流程，我只啟動了相機和推論節點，雷達和下位機都沒開。欸，相機居然正常了，深度和 RGB 都有。這個時候我還沒意識到差別在雷達，畢竟出發前的除錯裡它一直開著。於是我又半場開香檳，以為是什麼玄學問題，既然好了就先不管，安心睡了一會兒，等下午去現場除錯。

結果一進場館，一啟動完整流程，相機又掛了，深度依然斷流。這時我才想起中午沒有開雷達和下位機，開始逐一比對後，範圍終於縮小了：只要雷達上電並接入小電腦，相機深度就會中斷。我把現象告訴 gemini-3.8-flash，哈基米又開始應激，說可能是雷達的紅外光干擾了相機。我想，那天確實改過機械手臂的初始位置，雷達有可能掃到相機，而 D435 系列採用主動式雙目深度方案，也有紅外線投射器，光學干擾確實值得排查，於是我們把相機抬高，又用手遮住雷達測試，斷流仍然存在。直到換 gpt-6.1-sol 分析日誌，排查方向才終於轉到網路上：相機透過 USB 接入，並不代表 ROS 影像只走 USB，跨行程的原始影像流量可能正在經過雷達所在的百兆有線介面。後續限制 DDS 的業務組播後，深度恢復，網路埠傳送速率也明顯下降，這才把問題落到了通訊設定上。

## 根因剖析與傳輸機制

### 問題分析

現場最有力的證據，是故障與有線介面接入狀態、DDS 組播策略之間的對應關係：接上雷達網路後斷流，將 `AllowMulticast` 改為 `spdp` 後恢復，實體介面的傳送速率也從約 100 Mbps 降到 0.003 Mbps。這支持了**高頻寬影像透過 DDS 資料組播進入百兆鏈路，造成通訊壅塞**的解釋。

我換成 Cyclone DDS 後沒有立即遇到問題，是因為當時的通訊拓撲還比較簡單：相機與 YOLO 位於同一個容器行程內，在設定正確的情況下兩者可以走行程內通訊；後來新增的 WebRTC 節點在另一個行程中，需要透過 RMW/DDS 接收原始影像，於是多了一條高頻寬傳輸路徑（原本的行程內路徑並沒有因此失效）。Cyclone DDS 會根據介面能力、設定和發現到的對端選擇網路路徑。現場日誌中，無線介面出現過 `presumed flaky multicast, use for SPDP only`，有線介面則出現過 `presumed robust multicast support, use for everything`。這反映的是它對介面組播能力的預設判斷——無線介面傾向於只使用發現組播，有線介面則允許更廣泛地使用組播；這不等於「所有有線介面都會承載全部業務流量」，實際選擇還受版本、設定與訂閱拓撲影響。問題在於，允許資料組播的介面不一定有足夠頻寬：1280 × 720 的 RGB8 影像以 30 Hz 發布，僅像素有效負載就約為 664 Mbps，已經遠超這條 100 Mbps 鏈路，自然就會卡住。

![ROS 2 同機影像通訊與組播策略](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-ros-data-path-4c6bb401b377.png)

*圖 2：外部訂閱者增加了 DDS 影像傳輸路徑。改為 `spdp` 後，組播只用於參與者發現，端點匹配與影像傳輸使用單播；同機目的位址通常由本機路由交付，遠端訂閱者仍需要實體網路。*

> 還有一個反直覺的地方：資料明明已經透過 USB 進入同一台電腦，為什麼還會影響實體網路埠？因為跨行程通訊不會自動等於共享記憶體通訊。這裡使用的 DDS 網路路徑會把影像序列化後送入 UDP/IP 堆疊。向本機位址傳送單播時，Linux 通常透過本機路由交付；資料組播則可以同時產生面向實體介面的流量和本機回環交付。

## 解決方案

這次有效的修復，是把 Cyclone DDS 的組播限制在參與者發現階段，讓端點匹配和業務資料使用單播。在啟動 ROS 節點的終端機中設定：

```bash
export CYCLONEDDS_URI='<CycloneDDS><Domain Id="any"><General><AllowMulticast>spdp</AllowMulticast></General></Domain></CycloneDDS>'
```

也可以把它寫入 `~/.bashrc` 或 `~/.zshrc`，重新載入設定後再啟動相關節點。已經執行的行程不會自動取得新的環境變數，需要重新啟動；若節點由 systemd、容器或其他啟動器管理，也要在對應的啟動環境中傳入該變數。

`AllowMulticast` 取值說明

| 取值      | 行為與注意事項                                                              |
| :------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `true`  | 允許發現與使用者資料使用組播；是否實際使用還取決於介面和對端情況。在頻寬受限的網路上，需要檢查影像等大型話題的傳輸路徑。           |
| `false` | 停用該設定所控制的組播。預設的組播發現路徑不可用，可透過 `Peers` 等單播發現設定建立聯繫；不能概括為「任何節點發現都會徹底失效」。 |
| `spdp`  | 僅保留 SPDP 參與者發現組播，端點匹配和業務資料使用單播。本例中，它保留了方便的節點發現，也避免了向百兆介面傳送影像資料組播。    |

## 附錄

### 理論計算

#### 影像有效負載與百兆頻寬極限計算

當時一個很有用的線索，是 RGB 接收頻率只有 4.4 Hz 左右。從單幀大小反推，它的有效負載吞吐量已經接近 100 Mbps；實體網路埠的協商速率也恰好是 100 Mbps。這與鏈路成為瓶頸的解釋相符，但這個計算本身不能替代封包擷取或介面計數器。

| 影像串流 | 解析度 | 像素編碼 | 單幀資料量 | 30 Hz 理論頻寬 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| RGB | 1280 × 720 | RGB8（3 B/pixel） | 2.76 MB | **663.55 Mbps** |
| 原生深度 | 848 × 480 | Z16 / 16UC1（2 B/pixel） | 0.81 MB | **195.38 Mbps** |
| 對齊深度 | 1280 × 720 | 16UC1（2 B/pixel） | 1.84 MB | **442.37 Mbps** |

小電腦網路介面與雷達的實際協商速率為 **100 Mbps 全雙工**。全雙工表示兩個方向可以同時傳輸，並不會把單方向上限變成 200 Mbps。在不計任何協定開銷的理想情況下，它單方向最多容納：

$$100,000,000 \text{ bps} \div (1280 \times 720 \times 3 \times 8 \text{ bits}) \approx 4.52 \text{ fps}$$

現場 RGB 接收頻率為 **4.4 Hz**，換算出的像素有效負載約 **97.3 Mbps**，接近這一理論上限。

#### 實測資料對照驗證

| 監測指標 | 修復前 | 修復後 |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **彩色影像更新率** | 4.4 Hz | 13.9 Hz |
| **原生深度更新率** | 0 Hz | 29.7 Hz |
| **對齊深度更新率** | 0 Hz | 14.2 Hz |
| **RGBD 心跳頻率** | 0 Hz | 14.1 Hz |
| **彩色影像接收延遲中位數** | 943.9 ms | 58.3 ms |
| **原生深度接收延遲中位數** | N/A | 42.1 ms |
| **實體有線網路埠傳送速率** | 約 100 Mbps | **0.003 Mbps** |

恢復通訊不等於每路都跑滿 30 Hz：原生深度恢復到 29.7 Hz，但 RGB、對齊深度與 RGBD 心跳仍在 14 Hz 左右。這個結果說明斷流得到了緩解，不能據此聲稱整個視覺處理鏈路已經沒有其他瓶頸。

### DDS 介紹

![ROS 2 通訊分層與行程內路徑](https://img.muelsyse.us/bed/paper-20261110-ros-layers-24212fd3eca3.png)

*圖 5：ROS 2 的用戶端函式庫、RMW 與 DDS 通訊分層。符合條件的行程內路徑可以繞過 DDS 序列化；跨行程是否使用網路或共享記憶體，取決於所選實作及設定。*

DDS（Data Distribution Service）是 OMG 發布的分散式資料通訊標準。ROS 2 通常藉助 DDS 提供發現、發布訂閱和 QoS 等能力，透過 Topic 與資料型別組織通訊，並使用 **RMW（ROS Middleware Interface）** 將用戶端 API 與具體的中介軟體實作分開，從而能在介面支援的範圍內切換實作。與 ROS 1 常用的集中式 Master 發現方式相比，DDS 可以透過分散式發現建立端點聯繫（不過，ROS 1 的 Master 也不是所有業務資料的轉送中心；節點建立連線後，業務資料通常直接傳輸，不能把 Master 故障等同於所有既有資料連線立即中斷）。DDS 實作之間通常透過 RTPS 互通，UDP/IP 是常見傳輸方式，但 DDS 標準並非只允許這一種傳輸方式。

### Fast DDS vs Cyclone DDS

下表只整理與本次問題有關的差異，不依據這次現場經歷為兩種實作劃分絕對的適用情境。

| 評估維度 | Fast DDS | Cyclone DDS |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 共享記憶體 | 支援共享記憶體傳輸與資料共享等機制；是否啟用、是否減少序列化或複製，取決於版本、設定和訊息條件。 | 支援情況與版本、建置及設定有關；本文不能把「同機通訊」直接視為已啟用共享記憶體。 |
| 網路介面與組播 | 可設定網路傳輸、發現與組播行為，應檢查實際生效的設定。 | 有介面選擇和組播策略設定；本次透過 `AllowMulticast=spdp` 避免了業務資料組播。 |
| 本專案遇到的現象 | 曾遇到 Action / Service 不回應，未保留足夠資料確認具體機制。 | 外部影像訂閱與百兆有線介面加入後出現斷流，限制業務組播後恢復。 |
| 選型與驗證 | 應驗證具體版本下的功能、QoS、負載和故障復原。 | 同樣需要在完整節點拓撲與實際網路條件下驗證，不能只測單個節點。 |

### ROS 2 元件

ROS 2 元件將節點實作編譯為可動態載入的函式庫，由元件容器在同一個行程中載入。它提供共用的位址空間，便於組織節點，也為減少影像複製創造了條件，但容器如何排程回呼還取決於所選執行器，不能一概等同於「共用一個執行緒池」。相機發布、影像前處理、YOLO 推論這類連續處理大型訊息的節點，很適合檢查能否放入同一個容器中；不過，**元件化與行程內通訊是兩個相關但不同的設定點**，除了把節點放在一起，還要為相關節點啟用 `use_intra_process_comms`，並確認訊息與 QoS 支援這條路徑。

#### 元件化加速原理

滿足行程內通訊條件時，訊息可以透過 C++ 物件的所有權轉移或共享方式，交付給本機訂閱者，從而減少兩類開銷：

1. **訊息複製**：使用相容的發布與訂閱介面時，可以轉移 `std::unique_ptr` 或共享唯讀訊息；是否仍需複製，取決於訂閱者數量、回呼簽章和緩衝策略。
2. **序列化**：本機行程內交付可以繞過 DDS 的序列化與反序列化。若同時存在外部訂閱者，發布者仍需為外部路徑準備中介軟體訊息。

因此，「元件一開就完全零拷貝」不成立。要驗證實際效果，可以參考 ROS 2 的行程內通訊範例檢查訊息位址，再結合實際負載測量 CPU 使用量、記憶體頻寬和端到端延遲。

### 單播

單播會將資料傳送給特定目的位址。在本文的同機情境中，傳送至本機位址的資料通常可由本機路由交付，傳送至遠端主機則仍要使用實體鏈路。單播不會自動保證高吞吐量或低延遲，如果存在許多遠端訂閱者且需要分別傳送資料時，總流量反而可能增加；它在本例中的收益來自避免高頻寬業務組播進入受限介面。

### 組播

IPv4 組播使用 `224.0.0.0` 至 `239.255.255.255` 位址範圍。傳送端向組播群組傳送資料，網路設備按照組播轉送設定處理，接收端透過加入組播群組來接收；交換器是否只向有成員的連接埠轉送，還與 IGMP snooping 等功能有關，未啟用或設定不當時，流量可能被泛洪到更多連接埠。組播適合一對多傳輸，但仍然受鏈路頻寬、無線環境和端點實作限制。
